segments.text: Now that you clicked on the video of this UGC brief, I'm just going to quickly run over some really basic mistakes that a lot of UGC creators make and, you know, just improve your skills as a UGC creator. Now, I'm not looking to turn you into Leonardo DiCaprio or Zendaya, but these basic guidelines will make you better than half the stuff we sadly get nowadays. So, yeah, let's just quickly begin. Now, the most basic rule of thumb that you can think of is just keeping your face or the main action in the center of the screen. In this specific example, this was taken a bit too far.

Please don't do these super close-up shots. Of course, no blame to the UGC creator, but just don't do this. This really limits our options, and I'm not exactly sure what it's supposed to be to take here. So please just don't do this. Now, another thing you can do is just imagine a line between your face and the product.

because when you keep the product far away from your face you get shots like this where half of your body is out of frame the product is really low and point is there's nothing happening in the middle of the screen which is the main thing that's supposed to be happening so as a rule of thumb just keep the product near your face somewhere where the camera is at least in the center of the screen or the main actions happening at the center of the screen just your camera has those guidelines keep the square

everything like that if you're unsure if you're filming some clips then just put the phone in selfie mode and just go around and just experiment oh where does this product cut off and yeah just so you know roughly where it is just in general keep it near your face but of course don't cover your face and don't do weird shots like that now on the same theme of keeping things in center this guy in this shot actually is in center at least somewhat but a part of his action is out of frame now if you can

please capture the whole action whatever you're doing that is exercises stretching whatever sky's the limit honestly but please just capture the whole thing the whole action and if you can't really do it on the regular angle then try out the 0.5 model on your phone or the fisheye lens or whatever wide it is the one that makes it super wide just try that out it's better than nothing also yeah a couple things about color and contrast now you don't need to be

picasso or any artist to figure out that white on white is not a good combination you need to wear clothes in the b-roll or in general just filming that stick out from the background now i'm wearing a blue shirt and i have a chocolate brown background i stick out like a sore thumb plus i'm pale but in this example the guy is wearing a white shirt and a white background which is not optimal as i said you don't need to be an expert to spot that so please just switch out clothes it's written in the ugc brief but people just forget

can't blame them so yeah there's just something about color also about exposure if you're filming something that is super dark just bring it up a little lighter on the phone and let it adjust to the lighting just adjust the exposure because doing it post the production it becomes a bit difficult to make the footage look good so when you can just please tap it just check it make sure it's not too bright or too dark and that's pretty much it now you're qualified to make some good ugc videos so start filming thank you
